description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of various media outlets, likely representing their share of narrative framing in political discourse. The chart is divided into 18 distinct slices, which are visually arranged in descending order of size counter-clockwise, concluding with an aggregated "Other" category. The largest individual named slice is Breitbart (blue) at 14, followed by Drudge Report (orange) at 8, The Daily Caller (green) at 8, The Huffington Post (red) at 7, NPR (purple) at 6, and Vox (brown) at 6. Continuing counter-clockwise, The Guardian (pink) and BBC (grey) each account for 5, while RT (olive green) represents 4. A series of smaller slices, each labeled with a value of 3, includes Daily Kos (cyan), National Review (dark blue), Daily Mail (orange), Red State (green), Fox News (red), CNN (purple), PoliticusUSA (brown), and Shareblue (pink). Finally, the "Other" category (grey) accounts for 13 and is positioned adjacent to Breitbart, completing the circle. The chart does not utilize a separate legend; instead, the names of the media outlets are positioned outside the pie directly adjacent to their corresponding slices. Numerical values are displayed directly inside each slice, and none of the segments are visually emphasized through explosion, offsetting, or bolding.
